codes.title: Severe pre-eclampsia
codes.rationale: The patient is a 29-year-old female, 30+2 weeks pregnant, presenting with headache, visual disturbances, and significant hypertension (BP 168/112 and 165/110) with proteinuria (urine dipstick protein 3+). These findings meet the criteria for severe pre-eclampsia as defined in the guidelines.

evidence.quote: 29F, G2P1, 30+2 weeks by dating scan. Two days of headache across the forehead and flashing lights in her vision this morning. Swelling of hands and face noticed by her husband. BP 168/112, repeated after 15 minutes 165/110. Urine dipstick protein 3+.

New hypertension arising after twenty weeks of gestation with proteinuria, or with any of headache, visual disturbance, right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, hyperreflexia or a falling platelet count, is pre-eclampsia. The same hypertension after twenty weeks without proteinuria and without those features is gestational hypertension. Hypertension recorded before twenty weeks belongs to the chronic hypertension group carried into pregnancy. Severity features moving the assignment to the severe entry are systolic pressure at or above 160, platelets below 100, deranged transaminases, or pulmonary oedema.

confidence_rationale: The documented findings (headache, visual disturbances, significant hypertension, and proteinuria) clearly meet the criteria for severe pre-eclampsia as specified in the guidelines. No other condition in the catalogue accounts for these findings equally well.
